    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (I, J) tile updates a distinct TI x TJ submatrix of C; tiles are
    # independent because:
    #   - A and B are read-only,
    #   - C tiles are disjoint in memory.
    #
    # Parallelize across I (and optionally J) to use many cores.
    parallelize(I)
    # Optionally, also parallelize across J (e.g., using loop collapsing)
    # when NI is not large enough to saturate all cores by itself.
    # parallelize(J)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization along the reduction dimension k
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Thanks to the chosen layouts:
    #   - A[i, k] is contiguous in k for each fixed i (row-major),
    #   - B[k, j] is contiguous in k for each fixed j (column-major),
    # making the k-loop ideal for SIMD vectorization.
    #
    # For each (i, j), the scalar dot product:
    #   sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    # is implemented as a vectorized loop over k in chunks of VK, accumulating
    # partial sums in vector registers, followed by a horizontal reduction.
    vectorize(k, VK)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Loop unrolling in the j-dimension within each tile
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll j inside a tile to compute several C[i, j] values in parallel
    # and to better reuse A[i, k] across multiple columns of C:
    #
    #   for i in tile:
    #     for j in tile (unrolled by UJ):
    #       acc_j[0..UJ-1] = beta * C[i, j+offset]  // in registers
    #       for k in tile:
    #         a_ik = A[i, k]
    #         // see strength-reduction below for 'a_ik_scaled'
    #         acc_j[t] += alpha * a_ik * B[k, j+offset+t]
    #       C[i, j+offset+t] = acc_j[t]
    #
    # This encourages the compiler to keep multiple accumulators in registers
    # and to schedule FMAs efficiently.
    unroll(j, 4)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Arithmetic strength reduction and reuse
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside the innermost k-loop, the naive computation is:
    #   acc_ij += alpha * A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #
    # For each fixed (i, k) within a tile, we can hoist the multiplication
    # by alpha out of the j-loop:
    #
    #   a_ik_scaled = alpha * A[i, k]    # once per (i, k)
    #   acc_ij      += a_ik_scaled * B[k, j]
    #
    # This:
    #   - eliminates one multiply per (i, k, j),
    #   - exposes a simple multiply-add pattern that maps directly to a
    #     fused multiply-add (FMA) instruction:
    #       acc_ij = fma(a_ik_scaled, B[k, j], acc_ij)
    #
    # Implement a_ik_scaled as a scalar temporary in a register (no extra
    # array allocation, thus no extra asymptotic memory footprint).

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Fused beta scaling of C with the GEMM update
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The high-level assignment:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])
    #
    # replaces the original two passes:
    #   C[i, j] *= beta;
    #   C[i, j] += alpha * sum_k(...);
    #
    # Benefits:
    #   - C[i, j] is loaded once and stored once,
    #   - there is no separate "scaling-only" loop over C,
    #   - better opportunity to keep C[i, j] in a register during the entire
    #     k-reduction.

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7. Optional micro-kernel blocking within tiles
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # For further tuning on a specific x64 core, introduce a second level of
    # very small blocking inside each (i, j) tile, e.g.:
    #
    #   block(i, Ii, 4)
    #   block(j, Jj, 8)
    #   unroll(i, 4)
    #   unroll(j, 8)
    #
    # so that each 4x8 micro-tile of C is computed entirely in registers
    # before being written back to memory. This exploits the wide SIMD units
    # and the large register file typical of modern x64 cores, while the
    # outer (I, J, K) tiles manage cache locality.
--- END OF MODEL: gemm-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemm-02 ---
# Optimized model for PolyBench/C GEMM (kernel_gemm)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # rows of C and A
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # columns of C and B
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # shared / reduction dim

data:
    # Original inputs, row-major (PolyBench default).
    A[i, k]: in DATA_TYPE   = (i, k) -> i * NK + k
    B[k, j]: in DATA_TYPE   = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE= (i, j) -> i * NJ + j

    # Pre-scaled copy of A to hoist multiplication by alpha out of inner loops.
    # Size = NI * NK, i.e., +|A| extra storage ⇒
    #   (|A|+|B|+|C|) → (2|A|+|B|+|C|) = 4/3 of original for NI≈NJ≈NK (< 1.5×).
    A_alpha[i, k]: temp DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k  # row-major like A

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable transformation parameters (chosen w.r.t. cache sizes & SIMD width).
    TI: int  # tile size along i
    TJ: int  # tile size along j
    TK: int  # tile size along k
    VF: int  # vector width along j (e.g., 4, 8, 16 depending on SIMD)
    UK: int  # unroll factor for innermost k loop

computation:
    # 1) Pre-scale A once: A_alpha = alpha * A.
    #    This removes one multiplication from the inner GEMM loop for every (i,j,k).
    scale_A:
        for i, k:
            A_alpha[i, k] = alpha * A[i, k]

    # 2) Scale C by beta (matches the first loop in kernel_gemm).
    scale_C:
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    # 3) GEMM update: C += A_alpha * B.
    #    This is mathematically equivalent to the original:
    #      C_out[i,j] = beta * C_in[i,j] + alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j].
    gemm_update:
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = C[i, j] + sum(k, A_alpha[i, k] * B[k, j])

dependencies:
    # Pre-scaling of A and C must complete before using them in the GEMM update.
    for i in [0, NI), j in [0, NJ):
        scale_A(i) -> gemm_update(i, j)
        scale_C(i, j) -> gemm_update(i, j)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Cache-aware blocking (tiling)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile all three dimensions so that tiles of A_alpha (TI×TK) and B (TK×TJ)
    # fit in L2/L3, maximizing reuse and reducing bandwidth pressure.
    block(i, I, TI)   # I: outer tile index for rows of C/A/A_alpha
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J: outer tile index for cols of C/B
    block(k, K, TK)   # K: outer tile index for reduction dim

    # Conceptually, gemm_update becomes:
    # for I, J, K:
    #   for i in tile(I), j in tile(J):
    #     C[i, j] += sum(k in tile(K), A_alpha[i, k] * B[k, j])

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop ordering / hoisting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hoist K (reduction tiles) outward relative to inner i/j work to
    # improve reuse of A_alpha(I, K) and B(K, J) tiles across many C(I, J) updates.
    hoist(K)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelism
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelize over I-tiles (disjoint row blocks of C). There are no
    # cross-I dependencies: each I-tile updates different rows of C.
    parallelize(I)

    # Optionally, if NJ is large and NI is small, J can also be parallelized:
    # parallelize(J)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD vectorization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize along j (innermost within tiles) so that:
    #  - C[i, j] accesses are contiguous in memory,
    #  - B[k, j] accesses are contiguous for fixed k,
    # enabling efficient use of x64 SIMD (e.g., AVX2/AVX-512).
    vectorize(j, VF)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unrolling of reduction dimension
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the k loop inside each (i, j) tile to increase ILP
    # and to expose more opportunities for FMA instructions.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Additional arithmetic optimizations (implicit)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each (I, J, K) tile, the code generator is encouraged to:
    #  - keep A_alpha[i, k] in registers across the inner j-loop,
    #    i.e., compute a_k = A_alpha[i, k] once per (i, k) and reuse it:
    #       for k in tile(K):
    #         a_k = A_alpha[i, k]
    #         for j in tile(J):
    #             C[i, j] += a_k * B[k, j]
    #  - keep partial sums of C[i, j] in registers for the duration
    #    of the K-tile, reducing memory traffic on C.
--- END OF MODEL: gemm-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemm-03 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, NI)
    j: dim in [0, NJ)
    k: dim in [0, NK)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in row-major order, as in the original C code.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k      # A is NI x NK
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j      # B is NK x NJ
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j      # C is NI x NJ

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable performance parameters (constants at compile/run time):
    TI: int  # tile size in i (rows of A/C), e.g., 64–256
    TJ: int  # tile size in j (cols of B/C), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int  # tile size in k (inner dimension), e.g., 32–128

    VEC: int        # SIMD width in elements along j (e.g., 4 or 8 for double)
    UI:  int        # unroll factor in i inside a tile (small, e.g., 2–8)
    UK:  int        # unroll factor in k inside a tile (small, e.g., 2–8)
    NUM_THREADS: int  # number of worker threads (<= 32 physical cores)

computation:
    # Fused semantics of the original kernel:
    # For every element of C, first scale it by beta, then add the matrix product term.
    # sum(k, ...) is a reduction over k; for NK == 0, the sum is 0.
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])


optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse scaling and GEMM, stream C only once
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # The computation above already represents the fusion:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j] + alpha*sum_k(...)
    # so no separate pass over C is needed. This matches the original
    # behavior (scale then add A*B) but avoids an extra full sweep of C.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. 3D cache blocking (tiling) over i, j, k
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile all three dimensions so that each (TI x TJ) block of C and the
    # corresponding A- and B-tiles fit into cache.
    #
    # Conceptual loop nest after blocking and hoisting:
    #   for Ii in [0, NI) step TI       # outer tile in i
    #     for Jj in [0, NJ) step TJ     # outer tile in j
    #       for Kk in [0, NK) step TK   # tile in k (inner dimension)
    #         for i in tile(Ii)
    #           for k in tile(Kk)
    #             a_scaled = alpha * A[i, k]
    #             for j in tile(Jj)
    #               # on first Kk tile: incorporate beta*C; on others: accumulate
    #               C[i, j] = (Kk == 0 ? beta * C[i, j] : C[i, j]) + a_scaled * B[k, j]
    #
    # This structure reuses A[i,k] across many j in a tile, and B[k,j] across
    # many i in a tile, while keeping inner loops contiguous in memory.

    block(i, Ii, TI)    # split i into outer tile index Ii and inner i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)    # split j into outer tile index Jj and inner j
    block(k, Kk, TK)    # split k into outer tile index Kk and inner k

    # Hoist tile loops to the outside to form the 3-level blocked structure.
    hoist(Ii)           # outermost: tiles of rows of C/A
    hoist(Jj)           # next: tiles of columns of C/B
    hoist(Kk)           # then tiles of the shared k-dimension

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Loop ordering and SIMD
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each (Ii, Jj, Kk) tile, use loop order i -> k -> j:
    #   - j is innermost to make C[i,j] and B[k,j] accesses contiguous
    #     (row-major layout, stride-1 along j).
    #   - A[i,k] is loaded once per (i,k) and kept in a register for all j
    #     in the tile.
    #
    # Express this by ensuring j is the innermost dimension and vectorizing it.

    # Ensure j is innermost relative to k inside the tile.
    interchange(k, j)

    # Vectorize along j: load/store C[i, j..j+VEC) and B[k, j..j+VEC) with SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll over i and k within a tile to form a small register block:
    #   - UI: several rows of C updated together, reusing B[k,j] loaded once.
    #   - UK: several k-values unrolled to increase ILP and reuse C[i,j] in registers.
    unroll(i, UI)
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic strength reduction and register accumulators
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside the innermost (tile) nest, for fixed (i, k) we hoist the
    # multiplication by alpha:
    #
    #   a_scaled = alpha * A[i, k]
    #   for j in tile(Jj):
    #       C[i, j] += a_scaled * B[k, j]
    #
    # This replaces |tile(Jj)| multiplications by alpha per (i,k) with a single one.
    # Additionally, keep the partial sum for each C[i,j] element in a scalar
    # accumulator register while iterating over k, writing back to memory only
    # once per (i,j) element per Kk tile.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Parallelization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # C’s elements are independent across (i, j); k is a purely reduction
    # dimension. After blocking, each (Ii, Jj) tile of C is updated using
    # disjoint regions of C, so tiles can be processed in parallel without
    # synchronization or atomics.

    parallelize(Ii)     # distribute row-tiles of C across threads
    parallelize(Jj)     # optionally also distribute column-tiles if NJ is large

    # NUM_THREADS controls the degree of parallelism (e.g., up to 32 physical cores).
    # The runtime should schedule (Ii, Jj) tiles among NUM_THREADS worker threads,
    # ensuring each tile is owned by exactly one thread to avoid write conflicts.
--- END OF MODEL: gemm-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemm-04 ---
domain:
    # Logical iteration space of the GEMM kernel.
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # reduction index (shared dimension of A and B)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in row-major layout, consistent with the C code.
    # The affine expressions give the element's linear offset from the base.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k     # A is NI x NK
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j     # B is NK x NJ
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j     # C is NI x NJ

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking parameters for cache hierarchy (chosen at compile-time
    # or runtime; values below are recommendations for a modern x64 machine).
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of A, C)      e.g., TI = 64..128
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of B, C)      e.g., TJ = 64..128
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction dim)     e.g., TK = 64..256

    # SIMD and unrolling parameters (micro-kernel configuration).
    VEC_J: int  # SIMD vector width along j (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)
    UI:    int  # unroll factor along i inside a tile (e.g., 4)
    UK:    int  # unroll factor along k inside a tile (e.g., 4)

computation:
    gemm:
        # Semantics: for every (i, j),
        #   C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..NK-1} A[i,k] * B[k,j]
        #
        # This single assignment is mathematically equivalent to the original
        # PolyBench kernel, which first scales C by beta and then accumulates
        # alpha * A * B into C.
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. High-level loop structure and locality
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # We implement the above computation with a blocked 3D loop nest to exploit
    # temporal locality in A, B, and C and to match the cache hierarchy.
    #
    # Target logical loop order after transformations:
    #
    #   for I in 0 .. ceil(NI / TI):              # tile index in i
    #     for J in 0 .. ceil(NJ / TJ):            # tile index in j
    #       parallel over (I,J)
    #       # Work on a TI x TJ tile of C at a time
    #       for K in 0 .. ceil(NK / TK):          # tile index in k
    #         for i in tile I:
    #           for k in tile K:
    #             aik = alpha * A[i,k]            # scalar replacement
    #             for j in tile J (vectorized):
    #               # fused multiply-add into C
    #               C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j]  (only once per (i,j))  +
    #                          sum over all K-tiles of (aik * B[k,j])
    #
    # The directives below describe this schedule.

    # 3D blocking (tiling) for cache reuse: split each dimension into
    # an outer tile index (I,J,K) and an inner index (i,j,k).
    block(i, I, TI)   # I indexes tiles of TI consecutive rows of A and C
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J indexes tiles of TJ consecutive columns of B and C
    block(k, K, TK)   # K indexes tiles of TK elements along the reduction dim

    # Hoist tile loops to the outermost level so we iterate over tiles of C
    # and K-tiles of A,B before iterating over individual elements.
    # Resulting loop order (outermost -> innermost) is:
    #   I, J, K, i, k, j
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # Within each (I, J) C-tile, each (i, j) element of C is updated
    # independently over all k, so the computation over different tiles of C
    # can run in parallel without synchronization.
    #
    # We parallelize across tiles in I (rows). On a machine with many cores and
    # very large NJ, extending to 2D tile parallelism (I and J) is possible.
    parallelize(I)
    #parallelize(J)  # optional: 2D tile parallelism if NI is small and NJ large

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. SIMD vectorization and micro-kernel
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Make the innermost loop run along j, which is contiguous in memory for
    # both C[i,*] and B[k,*] (row-major), enabling efficient SIMD.
    #
    # The prior hoisting and blocking give innermost loops over (i,k,j);
    # we keep j as the innermost dimension inside the tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # Unroll short inner loops to form a small register-blocked micro-kernel
    # (e.g., computing UI x VEC_J elements of C in registers).
    unroll(i, UI)
    unroll(k, UK)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Arithmetic strength reduction and scalar replacement
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The expression alpha * A[i,k] does not depend on j and is reused across
    # the inner j loop of the blocked nest. We ensure it is computed only once
    # per (i,k) and kept in a scalar register.
    #
    # New directive (explained by this comment):
    #   scalar_replace(expr, scope, reused_across)
    #     - expr: expression to cache
    #     - scope: indices over which expr is defined once
    #     - reused_across: indices over which the cached value is reused
    scalar_replace(expr = alpha * A[i, k],
                   scope = (i, k),
                   reused_across = j)

    # Use fused multiply-add when available:
    #   C[i,j] = C[i,j] + aik * B[k,j]
    # becomes a single FMA instruction, reducing latency and improving
    # numerical accuracy (fewer rounding steps).
    #
    # New directive (explained by this comment):
    #   use_fma(update): implement the given update as a fused multiply-add.
    use_fma(update = C[i, j] += (alpha * A[i, k]) * B[k, j])

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Data alignment (implementation detail, not semantic)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Ensure matrices are allocated with 64-byte alignment to match cache-line
    # and SIMD alignment on modern x64, improving load/store efficiency.
    #
    # New directive:
    #   align(array, bytes): request that 'array' be aligned to 'bytes'.
    align(A, 64)
    align(B, 64)
    align(C, 64)
--- END OF MODEL: gemm-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: gemm-05 ---
domain:
    # Problem dimensions (as in the C kernel: ni, nj, nk)
    i: dim in [0, NI)
    j: dim in [0, NJ)
    k: dim in [0, NK)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in contiguous row-major order, exactly as in the C code.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k      # A[ni][nk]
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j      # B[nk][nj]
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j      # C[ni][nj]

    # Conceptual local tile of C; lives only inside a blocked kernel.
    # Implemented in registers or on the stack; does NOT increase asymptotic memory.
    C_tile[ii, jj]: local DATA_TYPE
      # ii in [0, TI), jj in [0, TJ)
      # Used to hold a TI×TJ sub-block of C while accumulating over k.

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking factors (chosen for the target cache hierarchy).
    TI: int  # block size along i (rows of A and C)
    TJ: int  # block size along j (columns of B and C)
    TK: int  # block size along k (shared inner dimension)

    # Tuning knobs for SIMD and ILP (instruction-level parallelism).
    VJ: int  # SIMD width along j (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double, 16 for AVX-512 float)
    UI: int  # unroll factor along i inside a tile

computation:
    # GEMM semantics:
    #   C := beta * C + alpha * A * B
    #
    # Expressed element-wise, matching the math of the original kernel:
    #   C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j] + alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #
    # (The original C code computes this via an outer scale by beta,
    #  followed by the triple-nested accumulation; this fused form is
    #  mathematically equivalent.)
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Three-dimensional blocking (tiling) for cache locality
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Split each logical loop dimension into an outer tile index (uppercase)
    # and an inner in-tile index (lowercase), with tile sizes TI, TJ, TK.
    #
    # i = I * TI + i_in   where i_in ≡ i (the renamed inner dim)
    # j = J * TJ + j_in
    # k = K * TK + k_in
    #
    # Remainder tiles (on the edges) are handled by partial tiles of smaller size.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    block(k, K, TK)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop reordering (schedule) to operate on a C tile at a time
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Target schedule (conceptually):
    #
    # for I:                      # outer tiles in i (rows)
    #   for J:                    # outer tiles in j (cols)
    #     # Load & beta-scale a TI×TJ tile of C into C_tile
    #     for i (inside tile I):
    #       for j (inside tile J):
    #         C_tile[i, j] = beta * C[I*TI + i, J*TJ + j]
    #
    #     # Accumulate contributions from the entire K dimension in blocks
    #     for K:
    #       for k (inside tile K):
    #         for i (inside tile I):
    #           a_ik = alpha * A[I*TI + i, K*TK + k]    # hoisted per-(i,k)
    #           for j (inside tile J):
    #             C_tile[i, j] += a_ik * B[K*TK + k, J*TJ + j]
    #
    #     # Write completed tile back to global C
    #     for i (inside tile I):
    #       for j (inside tile J):
    #         C[I*TI + i, J*TJ + j] = C_tile[i, j]
    #
    # This schedule:
    #   - Keeps a TI×TJ block of C in registers/L1 while sweeping over k.
    #   - Reads and writes each C element exactly once.
    #   - Reuses A and B blocks from faster caches.
    #
    # We express this intent by hoisting the tile indices outward:
    hoist(I)  # make I the outermost loop
    hoist(J)  # nest J immediately inside I
    hoist(K)  # nest K just inside (I, J), outside the inner i/j/k loops

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # All (i, j) pairs are independent; consequently, each (I, J) tile of C
    # is independent. We parallelize across the outer tile loops.
    #
    # The runtime may map (I, J) tiles to threads in a 1D or 2D partitioning,
    # e.g., collapse(I, J) and distribute, but semantically:
    #   - No synchronization is needed between different (I, J) tiles.
    #   - Each thread works on disjoint rows/columns of C.
    parallelize(I)   # primary parallel dimension: tiles over rows of C

    # Optionally also expose J for 2D tiling across threads, if desired.
    # (This is safe as long as the parallel runtime does not create nested
    #  parallel regions that oversubscribe cores.)
    parallelize(J)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization along j (inner-most column index)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # In row-major layout:
    #   - For both B and C, the j index is contiguous in memory.
    #   - Vectorizing along j (the in-tile 'j' after blocking) gives
    #     unit-stride accesses for C and B and good use of SIMD units.
    #
    # The vectorization width VJ is tuned to the ISA (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double).
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Loop unrolling for ILP and FMA utilization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the inner i loop (rows within a tile) to expose ILP and allow
    # the compiler to map multiple independent accumulators to registers.
    unroll(i, UI)
    # Additionally unroll the inner k loop in the micro-kernel; a small fixed
    # factor (e.g., 4 or 8) works well in practice and is easily tuned.
    unroll(k, 4)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Use of local accumulation variables and strength reduction
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside the innermost micro-kernel (after tiling and scheduling), the
    # compiler is instructed/allowed to:
    #
    # - Use a local accumulator per (i, j) entry in the current tile:
    #       acc_ij = beta * C[i, j]
    #       acc_ij += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #       C[i, j] = acc_ij
    #   or equivalently with the C_tile buffer:
    #       C_tile[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #       C_tile[i, j] += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #       C[i, j] = C_tile[i, j]
    #
    #   This ensures:
    #     * Each C[i, j] is loaded once, stored once.
    #     * All k-contributions are accumulated in registers.
    #
    # - Hoist alpha * A[i, k] out of the innermost j loop:
    #       a_ik = alpha * A[i, k]
    #       for j:
    #           C_tile[i, j] += a_ik * B[k, j]
    #
    #   This replaces multiple multiplications by alpha with a single one
    #   per (i, k) pair and reuses a_ik for all j, which is exactly the
    #   optimization a good compiler will derive from this schedule.
    #
    # These transformations are consistent with the high-level assignment
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])
    # and do not change the mathematical result (only the order of FP
    # operations and thus round-off at machine precision).

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7. Memory usage constraints and layout
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The only additional storage is the per-tile C_tile[ii, jj], whose
    #   size is TI × TJ and thus negligible compared to A, B, and C.
    #   This increases total memory usage by << 50%.
    #
    # - The global layouts of A, B, and C remain row-major and unchanged
    #   relative to the original C code, so no changes to initialization
    #   or I/O are required.

/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>
 *

 */
/* gemm.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "gemm.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int ni, int nj, int nk,
		DATA_TYPE *alpha,
		DATA_TYPE *beta,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NI,NJ,ni,nj),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj))
{
  int i, j;

  *alpha = 1.5;
  *beta = 1.2;
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++)
      C[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j+1) % ni) / ni;
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nk; j++)
      A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+1) % nk) / nk;
  for (i = 0; i < nk; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++)
      B[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*(j+2) % nj) / nj;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int ni, int nj,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NI,NJ,ni,nj))
{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("C");
  for (i = 0; i < ni; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nj; j++) {
	if ((i * ni + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, C[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("C");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_gemm[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int ni, int nj, int nk,
		 DATA_TYPE alpha,
		 DATA_TYPE beta,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C,NI,NJ,ni,nj),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,NI,NK,ni,nk),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(B,NK,NJ,nk,nj))
{
  int i, j, k;

//BLAS PARAMS
//TRANSA = 'N'
//TRANSB = 'N'
// => Form C := alpha*A*B + beta*C,
//A is NIxNK
//B is NKxNJ
//C is NIxNJ
#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_NI; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_NJ; j++)
	C[i][j] *= beta;
    for (k = 0; k < _PB_NK; k++) {
       for (j = 0; j < _PB_NJ; j++)
	  C[i][j] += alpha * A[i][k] * B[k][j];
    }
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int ni = NI;
  int nj = NJ;
  int nk = NK;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE alpha;
  DATA_TYPE beta;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C,DATA_TYPE,NI,NJ,ni,nj);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NI,NK,ni,nk);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B,DATA_TYPE,NK,NJ,nk,nj);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (ni, nj, nk, &alpha, &beta,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_gemm (ni, nj, nk,
	       alpha, beta,
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	       POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(ni, nj,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

  return 0;
}

    #   C := beta * C + alpha * A * B

    # Expressed in a single assignment so that for each (i, j) the
    # accumulator remains in a register across the k-reduction:
    #
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]

    #   C[i, j] *= beta;
    #   C[i, j] += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j];

    # of C inside the k-loop.

    #   - a loop over k for each fixed (i, j),
    #   - an implicit dependence along k for each (i, j),
    #   - full independence across different (i, j) pairs.
    gemm:
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] +

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile the iteration space so that:

    #   - B tile: TK x TJ
    #   - C tile: TI x TJ
    block(i, I, TI)   # i = I * TI + i_inner
    block(j, J, TJ)   # j = J * TJ + j_inner
    block(k, K, TK)   # k = K * TK + k_inner

    #     for J         // outer tiles over cols of C/B
    #       for K       // tiles along reduction dimension

    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    TJ: int  # tile size along j
    TK: int  # tile size along k
    VF: int  # vector width along j (e.g., 4, 8, 16 depending on SIMD)
    UK: int  # unroll factor for innermost k loop

    #    This removes one multiplication from the inner GEMM loop for every (i,j,k).

domain:
    i: dim in [0, NI)
    j: dim in [0, NJ)
    k: dim in [0, NK)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in row-major order, as in the original C code.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k      # A is NI x NK
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j      # B is NK x NJ
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j      # C is NI x NJ

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable performance parameters (constants at compile/run time):
    TI: int  # tile size in i (rows of A/C), e.g., 64–256
    TJ: int  # tile size in j (cols of B/C), e.g., 64–256
    TK: int  # tile size in k (inner dimension), e.g., 32–128

    VEC: int        # SIMD width in elements along j (e.g., 4 or 8 for double)
    UI:  int        # unroll factor in i inside a tile (small, e.g., 2–8)
    UK:  int        # unroll factor in k inside a tile (small, e.g., 2–8)
    NUM_THREADS: int  # number of worker threads (<= 32 physical cores)

computation:
    # Fused semantics of the original kernel:
    # For every element of C, first scale it by beta, then add the matrix product term.
    # sum(k, ...) is a reduction over k; for NK == 0, the sum is 0.
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])


optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Fuse scaling and GEMM, stream C only once
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # The computation above already represents the fusion:
    #   C[i,j] = beta*C[i,j] + alpha*sum_k(...)
    # so no separate pass over C is needed. This matches the original
    # behavior (scale then add A*B) but avoids an extra full sweep of C.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. 3D cache blocking (tiling) over i, j, k
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile all three dimensions so that each (TI x TJ) block of C and the
    # corresponding A- and B-tiles fit into cache.
    #
    # Conceptual loop nest after blocking and hoisting:
    #   for Ii in [0, NI) step TI       # outer tile in i
    #     for Jj in [0, NJ) step TJ     # outer tile in j
    #       for Kk in [0, NK) step TK   # tile in k (inner dimension)
    #         for i in tile(Ii)
    #           for k in tile(Kk)
    #             a_scaled = alpha * A[i, k]
    #             for j in tile(Jj)
    #               # on first Kk tile: incorporate beta*C; on others: accumulate
    #               C[i, j] = (Kk == 0 ? beta * C[i, j] : C[i, j]) + a_scaled * B[k, j]
    #
    # This structure reuses A[i,k] across many j in a tile, and B[k,j] across
    # many i in a tile, while keeping inner loops contiguous in memory.

    block(i, Ii, TI)    # split i into outer tile index Ii and inner i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)    # split j into outer tile index Jj and inner j
    block(k, Kk, TK)    # split k into outer tile index Kk and inner k

    # Hoist tile loops to the outside to form the 3-level blocked structure.
    hoist(Ii)           # outermost: tiles of rows of C/A
    hoist(Jj)           # next: tiles of columns of C/B
    hoist(Kk)           # then tiles of the shared k-dimension

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Loop ordering and SIMD
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each (Ii, Jj, Kk) tile, use loop order i -> k -> j:
    #   - j is innermost to make C[i,j] and B[k,j] accesses contiguous
    #     (row-major layout, stride-1 along j).
    #   - A[i,k] is loaded once per (i,k) and kept in a register for all j
    #     in the tile.
    #
    # Express this by ensuring j is the innermost dimension and vectorizing it.

    # Ensure j is innermost relative to k inside the tile.
    interchange(k, j)

    # Vectorize along j: load/store C[i, j..j+VEC) and B[k, j..j+VEC) with SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VEC)

    # Unroll over i and k within a tile to form a small register block:
    #   - UI: several rows of C updated together, reusing B[k,j] loaded once.
    #   - UK: several k-values unrolled to increase ILP and reuse C[i,j] in registers.
    unroll(i, UI)
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic strength reduction and register accumulators
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside the innermost (tile) nest, for fixed (i, k) we hoist the
    # multiplication by alpha:
    #
    #   a_scaled = alpha * A[i, k]
    #   for j in tile(Jj):
    #       C[i, j] += a_scaled * B[k, j]
    #
    # This replaces |tile(Jj)| multiplications by alpha per (i,k) with a single one.
    # Additionally, keep the partial sum for each C[i,j] element in a scalar
    # accumulator register while iterating over k, writing back to memory only
    # once per (i,j) element per Kk tile.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Parallelization
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # C’s elements are independent across (i, j); k is a purely reduction
    # dimension. After blocking, each (Ii, Jj) tile of C is updated using
    # disjoint regions of C, so tiles can be processed in parallel without
    # synchronization or atomics.

    parallelize(Ii)     # distribute row-tiles of C across threads
    parallelize(Jj)     # optionally also distribute column-tiles if NJ is large

    # NUM_THREADS controls the degree of parallelism (e.g., up to 32 physical cores).
    # The runtime should schedule (Ii, Jj) tiles among NUM_THREADS worker threads,
    # ensuring each tile is owned by exactly one thread to avoid write conflicts.

domain:
    # Logical iteration space of the GEMM kernel.
    i: dim in [0, NI)   # row index of A and C
    j: dim in [0, NJ)   # column index of B and C
    k: dim in [0, NK)   # reduction index (shared dimension of A and B)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in row-major layout, consistent with the C code.
    # The affine expressions give the element's linear offset from the base.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k     # A is NI x NK
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j     # B is NK x NJ
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j     # C is NI x NJ

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking parameters for cache hierarchy (chosen at compile-time
    # or runtime; values below are recommendations for a modern x64 machine).
    TI: int  # tile size along i (rows of A, C)      e.g., TI = 64..128
    TJ: int  # tile size along j (cols of B, C)      e.g., TJ = 64..128
    TK: int  # tile size along k (reduction dim)     e.g., TK = 64..256

    # SIMD and unrolling parameters (micro-kernel configuration).
    VEC_J: int  # SIMD vector width along j (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)
    UI:    int  # unroll factor along i inside a tile (e.g., 4)
    UK:    int  # unroll factor along k inside a tile (e.g., 4)

computation:
    gemm:
        # Semantics: for every (i, j),
        #   C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j] + alpha * sum_{k=0..NK-1} A[i,k] * B[k,j]
        #
        # This single assignment is mathematically equivalent to the original
        # PolyBench kernel, which first scales C by beta and then accumulates
        # alpha * A * B into C.
        for i, j:
            C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. High-level loop structure and locality
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # We implement the above computation with a blocked 3D loop nest to exploit
    # temporal locality in A, B, and C and to match the cache hierarchy.
    #
    # Target logical loop order after transformations:
    #
    #   for I in 0 .. ceil(NI / TI):              # tile index in i
    #     for J in 0 .. ceil(NJ / TJ):            # tile index in j
    #       parallel over (I,J)
    #       # Work on a TI x TJ tile of C at a time
    #       for K in 0 .. ceil(NK / TK):          # tile index in k
    #         for i in tile I:
    #           for k in tile K:
    #             aik = alpha * A[i,k]            # scalar replacement
    #             for j in tile J (vectorized):
    #               # fused multiply-add into C
    #               C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j]  (only once per (i,j))  +
    #                          sum over all K-tiles of (aik * B[k,j])
    #
    # The directives below describe this schedule.

    # 3D blocking (tiling) for cache reuse: split each dimension into
    # an outer tile index (I,J,K) and an inner index (i,j,k).
    block(i, I, TI)   # I indexes tiles of TI consecutive rows of A and C
    block(j, J, TJ)   # J indexes tiles of TJ consecutive columns of B and C
    block(k, K, TK)   # K indexes tiles of TK elements along the reduction dim

    # Hoist tile loops to the outermost level so we iterate over tiles of C
    # and K-tiles of A,B before iterating over individual elements.
    # Resulting loop order (outermost -> innermost) is:
    #   I, J, K, i, k, j
    hoist(I)
    hoist(J)
    hoist(K)

    # Within each (I, J) C-tile, each (i, j) element of C is updated
    # independently over all k, so the computation over different tiles of C
    # can run in parallel without synchronization.
    #
    # We parallelize across tiles in I (rows). On a machine with many cores and
    # very large NJ, extending to 2D tile parallelism (I and J) is possible.
    parallelize(I)
    #parallelize(J)  # optional: 2D tile parallelism if NI is small and NJ large

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. SIMD vectorization and micro-kernel
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Make the innermost loop run along j, which is contiguous in memory for
    # both C[i,*] and B[k,*] (row-major), enabling efficient SIMD.
    #
    # The prior hoisting and blocking give innermost loops over (i,k,j);
    # we keep j as the innermost dimension inside the tile.
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # Unroll short inner loops to form a small register-blocked micro-kernel
    # (e.g., computing UI x VEC_J elements of C in registers).
    unroll(i, UI)
    unroll(k, UK)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Arithmetic strength reduction and scalar replacement
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The expression alpha * A[i,k] does not depend on j and is reused across
    # the inner j loop of the blocked nest. We ensure it is computed only once
    # per (i,k) and kept in a scalar register.
    #
    # New directive (explained by this comment):
    #   scalar_replace(expr, scope, reused_across)
    #     - expr: expression to cache
    #     - scope: indices over which expr is defined once
    #     - reused_across: indices over which the cached value is reused
    scalar_replace(expr = alpha * A[i, k],
                   scope = (i, k),
                   reused_across = j)

    # Use fused multiply-add when available:
    #   C[i,j] = C[i,j] + aik * B[k,j]
    # becomes a single FMA instruction, reducing latency and improving
    # numerical accuracy (fewer rounding steps).
    #
    # New directive (explained by this comment):
    #   use_fma(update): implement the given update as a fused multiply-add.
    use_fma(update = C[i, j] += (alpha * A[i, k]) * B[k, j])

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Data alignment (implementation detail, not semantic)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Ensure matrices are allocated with 64-byte alignment to match cache-line
    # and SIMD alignment on modern x64, improving load/store efficiency.
    #
    # New directive:
    #   align(array, bytes): request that 'array' be aligned to 'bytes'.
    align(A, 64)
    align(B, 64)
    align(C, 64)

--- START OF MODEL: gemm-05 ---
domain:
    # Problem dimensions (as in the C kernel: ni, nj, nk)
    i: dim in [0, NI)
    j: dim in [0, NJ)
    k: dim in [0, NK)

data:
    # All matrices are stored in contiguous row-major order, exactly as in the C code.
    A[i, k]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i, k) -> i * NK + k      # A[ni][nk]
    B[k, j]: in    DATA_TYPE = (k, j) -> k * NJ + j      # B[nk][nj]
    C[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * NJ + j      # C[ni][nj]

    # Conceptual local tile of C; lives only inside a blocked kernel.
    # Implemented in registers or on the stack; does NOT increase asymptotic memory.
    C_tile[ii, jj]: local DATA_TYPE
      # ii in [0, TI), jj in [0, TJ)
      # Used to hold a TI×TJ sub-block of C while accumulating over k.

parameters:
    alpha: DATA_TYPE
    beta:  DATA_TYPE

    # Tunable blocking factors (chosen for the target cache hierarchy).
    TI: int  # block size along i (rows of A and C)
    TJ: int  # block size along j (columns of B and C)
    TK: int  # block size along k (shared inner dimension)

    # Tuning knobs for SIMD and ILP (instruction-level parallelism).
    VJ: int  # SIMD width along j (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double, 16 for AVX-512 float)
    UI: int  # unroll factor along i inside a tile

computation:
    # GEMM semantics:
    #   C := beta * C + alpha * A * B
    #
    # Expressed element-wise, matching the math of the original kernel:
    #   C[i,j] = beta * C[i,j] + alpha * sum_k A[i,k] * B[k,j]
    #
    # (The original C code computes this via an outer scale by beta,
    #  followed by the triple-nested accumulation; this fused form is
    #  mathematically equivalent.)
    for i, j:
        C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Three-dimensional blocking (tiling) for cache locality
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Split each logical loop dimension into an outer tile index (uppercase)
    # and an inner in-tile index (lowercase), with tile sizes TI, TJ, TK.
    #
    # i = I * TI + i_in   where i_in ≡ i (the renamed inner dim)
    # j = J * TJ + j_in
    # k = K * TK + k_in
    #
    # Remainder tiles (on the edges) are handled by partial tiles of smaller size.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    block(k, K, TK)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Loop reordering (schedule) to operate on a C tile at a time
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Target schedule (conceptually):
    #
    # for I:                      # outer tiles in i (rows)
    #   for J:                    # outer tiles in j (cols)
    #     # Load & beta-scale a TI×TJ tile of C into C_tile
    #     for i (inside tile I):
    #       for j (inside tile J):
    #         C_tile[i, j] = beta * C[I*TI + i, J*TJ + j]
    #
    #     # Accumulate contributions from the entire K dimension in blocks
    #     for K:
    #       for k (inside tile K):
    #         for i (inside tile I):
    #           a_ik = alpha * A[I*TI + i, K*TK + k]    # hoisted per-(i,k)
    #           for j (inside tile J):
    #             C_tile[i, j] += a_ik * B[K*TK + k, J*TJ + j]
    #
    #     # Write completed tile back to global C
    #     for i (inside tile I):
    #       for j (inside tile J):
    #         C[I*TI + i, J*TJ + j] = C_tile[i, j]
    #
    # This schedule:
    #   - Keeps a TI×TJ block of C in registers/L1 while sweeping over k.
    #   - Reads and writes each C element exactly once.
    #   - Reuses A and B blocks from faster caches.
    #
    # We express this intent by hoisting the tile indices outward:
    hoist(I)  # make I the outermost loop
    hoist(J)  # nest J immediately inside I
    hoist(K)  # nest K just inside (I, J), outside the inner i/j/k loops

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # All (i, j) pairs are independent; consequently, each (I, J) tile of C
    # is independent. We parallelize across the outer tile loops.
    #
    # The runtime may map (I, J) tiles to threads in a 1D or 2D partitioning,
    # e.g., collapse(I, J) and distribute, but semantically:
    #   - No synchronization is needed between different (I, J) tiles.
    #   - Each thread works on disjoint rows/columns of C.
    parallelize(I)   # primary parallel dimension: tiles over rows of C

    # Optionally also expose J for 2D tiling across threads, if desired.
    # (This is safe as long as the parallel runtime does not create nested
    #  parallel regions that oversubscribe cores.)
    parallelize(J)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization along j (inner-most column index)
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # In row-major layout:
    #   - For both B and C, the j index is contiguous in memory.
    #   - Vectorizing along j (the in-tile 'j' after blocking) gives
    #     unit-stride accesses for C and B and good use of SIMD units.
    #
    # The vectorization width VJ is tuned to the ISA (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double).
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Loop unrolling for ILP and FMA utilization
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the inner i loop (rows within a tile) to expose ILP and allow
    # the compiler to map multiple independent accumulators to registers.
    unroll(i, UI)
    # Additionally unroll the inner k loop in the micro-kernel; a small fixed
    # factor (e.g., 4 or 8) works well in practice and is easily tuned.
    unroll(k, 4)

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Use of local accumulation variables and strength reduction
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # Inside the innermost micro-kernel (after tiling and scheduling), the
    # compiler is instructed/allowed to:
    #
    # - Use a local accumulator per (i, j) entry in the current tile:
    #       acc_ij = beta * C[i, j]
    #       acc_ij += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #       C[i, j] = acc_ij
    #   or equivalently with the C_tile buffer:
    #       C_tile[i, j] = beta * C[i, j]
    #       C_tile[i, j] += alpha * sum_k A[i, k] * B[k, j]
    #       C[i, j] = C_tile[i, j]
    #
    #   This ensures:
    #     * Each C[i, j] is loaded once, stored once.
    #     * All k-contributions are accumulated in registers.
    #
    # - Hoist alpha * A[i, k] out of the innermost j loop:
    #       a_ik = alpha * A[i, k]
    #       for j:
    #           C_tile[i, j] += a_ik * B[k, j]
    #
    #   This replaces multiple multiplications by alpha with a single one
    #   per (i, k) pair and reuses a_ik for all j, which is exactly the
    #   optimization a good compiler will derive from this schedule.
    #
    # These transformations are consistent with the high-level assignment
    #   C[i, j] = beta * C[i, j] + alpha * sum(k, A[i, k] * B[k, j])
    # and do not change the mathematical result (only the order of FP
    # operations and thus round-off at machine precision).

    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # 7. Memory usage constraints and layout
    #------------------------------------------------------------
    # - The only additional storage is the per-tile C_tile[ii, jj], whose
    #   size is TI × TJ and thus negligible compared to A, B, and C.
    #   This increases total memory usage by << 50%.
    #
    # - The global layouts of A, B, and C remain row-major and unchanged
    #   relative to the original C code, so no changes to initialization
    #   or I/O are required.

/* heat-3d.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "heat-3d.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,N,N,N,n,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(B,N,N,N,n,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < n; k++)
        A[i][j][k] = B[i][j][k] = (DATA_TYPE) (i + j + (n-k))* 10 / (n);
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,N,N,N,n,n,n))

{
  int i, j, k;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < n; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < n; k++) {
         if ((i * n * n + j * n + k) % 20 == 0) fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
         fprintf(POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j][k]);
      }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_heat_3d[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int tsteps,
		      int n,
		      DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,N,N,N,n,n,n),
		      DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(B,N,N,N,n,n,n))
{
  int t, i, j, k;

#pragma scop
    for (t = 1; t <= TSTEPS; t++) {
        for (i = 1; i < _PB_N-1; i++) {
            for (j = 1; j < _PB_N-1; j++) {
                for (k = 1; k < _PB_N-1; k++) {
                    B[i][j][k] =   SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (A[i+1][j][k] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * A[i][j][k] + A[i-1][j][k])
                                 + SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (A[i][j+1][k] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * A[i][j][k] + A[i][j-1][k])
                                 + SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (A[i][j][k+1] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * A[i][j][k] + A[i][j][k-1])
                                 + A[i][j][k];
                }
            }
        }
        for (i = 1; i < _PB_N-1; i++) {
           for (j = 1; j < _PB_N-1; j++) {
               for (k = 1; k < _PB_N-1; k++) {
                   A[i][j][k] =   SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (B[i+1][j][k] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * B[i][j][k] + B[i-1][j][k])
                                + SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (B[i][j+1][k] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * B[i][j][k] + B[i][j-1][k])
                                + SCALAR_VAL(0.125) * (B[i][j][k+1] - SCALAR_VAL(2.0) * B[i][j][k] + B[i][j][k-1])
                                + B[i][j][k];
               }
           }
       }
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int tsteps = TSTEPS;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, N, n, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, N, n, n, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_heat_3d (tsteps, n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A), POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}
